title: Quantum Processor GPU Replacement — Research and Experiment Program
objective: Investigate whether quantum processing can replace GPU compute capability for accepted workload families, prioritizing fewer logical qubits while evaluating total physical and system resources.

hypotheses.claim: At least one practical workload family has an end-to-end QPU advantage over the strongest fair GPU baseline.
hypotheses.falsifier: No crossover after input encoding, QEC, shots, readout, host and system costs.

hypotheses.claim: A small logical-qubit register can represent and process selected useful tasks more efficiently.
hypotheses.falsifier: State preparation, oracle, ancilla, precision, QEC or output costs erase the benefit.

hypotheses.claim: Block encoding/QSVT or quantum linear solvers can outperform GPUs on selected structured matrix tasks.
hypotheses.falsifier: No crossover for the frozen matrix families and requested output contract.

hypotheses.claim: Quantum search/optimization improves accepted solution quality per total resource on selected families.
hypotheses.falsifier: No credible gain under equal objective, quality and tuning/shot budgets.

hypotheses.claim: Amplitude estimation reduces total cost for selected sampling tasks at equal error/confidence.
hypotheses.falsifier: Circuit and state-preparation costs exceed classical variance-reduced methods.

hypotheses.claim: Quantum-native representations can replace selected AI kernels or graphs at matched quality.
Algorithm/compiler/device co-design reduces full-stack resource requirements.
hypotheses.falsifier: Savings fail to survive physical mapping and system accounting.

hypotheses.claim: Optimized classical systems dominate the tested workload and size range.
hypotheses.falsifier: A reproducible QPU advantage passes all gates.

open_questions: Q-003 compact output versus full output
Q-007 circuit depth and two-qubit gate reduction
Q-014 useful family coverage with few qubits
Q-017 complete AI graph without hidden GPU
Q-018 workload scope outside quantum candidate
qubit_count_semantics: logical_qubits; physical_qubits and QEC overhead must be estimated separately
comparison_rules: include state preparation and input/oracle access
evidence_boundary: No experiments, GPU measurements, QPU jobs, hardware claims or quantum advantage are asserted by this preregistration.
next_action: Freeze EXP-00 and EXP-01 contracts, then select one EXP-05 structured matrix workload and reuse the existing signed-Max-Cut held-out fixtures for EXP-06.
